task.title: Run OpenD on Railway
task.shortdesc: One Railway project runs one OpenD instance: a web service, a worker, Postgres and a bucket.

context.p: On Railway the web service and the worker are separate services that cannot share a disk, so blobs go to a Railway Bucket. Railway has deprecated railway.json, so apply the settings below per service, in the dashboard or through the Railway API. See for the platform itself.

step.cmd: Create a project and add Postgres and a Bucket.
Add two services from this repository, web and worker, both building deploy/Dockerfile, and configure them.

info.p: A start command replaces the image's entry point, so always give the full node dist/bin.js <command>. Watch paths keep docs-only commits from redeploying the app: docs reach readers through the worker, not through a redeploy.

step.cmd: Set the variables on both services, using reference variables for Postgres and the bucket.

info.p: Replace Bucket with your bucket service's name. Railway buckets use virtual-hosted addressing, so leave S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE unset. Add the OIDC_* variables for reader sign-in, and OPEND_EMBED_SECRET and OPEND_EMBED_ORIGINS to embed help in your apps.

step.cmd: Deploy, and wait for web to report healthy.

info.p: Its pre-deploy step creates the schema. The worker retries until the schema exists.

step.cmd: Register the docs repository, and add organizations and readers, through the admin API.
Publish: point a GitHub webhook at $PUBLIC_URL/webhooks/github, or trigger a build directly.

stepxmp.codeblock: curl -X POST "$PUBLIC_URL/admin/api/repos/1/builds" -H "authorization: Bearer $OPEND_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"ref":"main","sha":"<full commit sha>"}'

result.p: A public demo can set NODE_ENV=development and OPEND_DEV_LOGIN=1 so visitors pick a sample reader. Never do this with real content.
To add the web editor, create a third service from the same Dockerfile with the start command node dist/bin.js editor serve and its own domain. See .
Tagged releases are published as images to , so a service can deploy an image tag instead of building from the repository.
